event: Every OpenAI cloud dispatch from opencode failed with Bad Request: {"detail":"Unsupported parameter: max_output_tokens"} starting 2026-09-04T22:01Z, after the cost-router chat.params hook began setting output.maxOutputTokens on every request.
why_chain: Requests failed because opencode's OpenAI OAuth path sends chat completions to the ChatGPT Codex backend (https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses), a FastAPI service that rejects the wire parameter max_output_tokens for gpt-5.6-* models.

The Responses/Codex request builder in opencode 1.18.19 includes max_output_tokens in the request body whenever maxOutputTokens is set ($.maxOutputTokens||this.config.maxTokens||8192), so every request carried the rejected parameter.

The cost-router plugin's chat.params hook (added 2026-09-04T21:36Z) set output.maxOutputTokens = min(existing, decision.max_output_tokens) on every dispatch to enforce the usage-policy output_limits (2048/4096/8192), which converted a previously-tolerated default into an always-present parameter.

Before the hook, opencode core still computed a maxOutputTokens internally (min(model limit, 32000) via its own cap function), and the backend accepted those requests (524 openai successes on 2026-09-04 before 21:36Z; zero max_output_tokens rejections in the prior 30 days), so the parameter reached the wire then too but the backend only began enforcing its rejection for the gpt-5.6 family after ~2026-09-04T22:01Z; the hook made every request fail deterministically instead of conditionally.

No pre-dispatch compatibility check existed between the plugin's wire-level parameter choices and the backend's accepted-parameter set, so a backend-side contract change or a plugin override could break every OpenAI request without any circuit or fallback catching it at dispatch time.
root_cause: The cost-router plugin enforced its output-token budget by setting maxOutputTokens on the OpenAI chat params, but the ChatGPT Codex OAuth backend rejects the max_output_tokens wire parameter for gpt-5.6 models, so every OpenAI dispatch after the hook landed returned Bad Request.
contributing_factors: The output_limits budget was already enforced at reservation time (assertDispatchAllowed computes projected charges from the tier output limit), so setting maxOutputTokens on the wire added redundant enforcement, not new protection.

opencode 1.18.19's Responses path unconditionally includes max_output_tokens once maxOutputTokens is set, with no 400-retry fallback (it only retries token-auth errors), so a rejected parameter fails every request in the session.
The error body {"detail":...} is FastAPI-style from the Codex backend rather than OpenAI's standard {"error":{...}} shape, which initially obscured which service rejected the request.
immediate_correction: Stop setting maxOutputTokens in the chat.params hook for the openai provider (the Codex backend rejects the derived wire parameter); keep the existing reservation-time budget enforcement, which already bounds projected output cost before dispatch.
root_cause_correction: The plugin enforces output budgets only through its dispatch-time reservation (assertDispatchAllowed + reserveDispatch), never by mutating provider wire parameters; provider-specific request shaping is left to opencode core, which knows each provider's accepted parameter set.
mechanical_recurrence_guard: The usage-ledger test suite gains a regression test asserting that reserveDispatch/assertDispatchAllowed decisions carry no wire-parameter mutation contract, and cost-router's chat.params hook is restricted to providers whose backends accept the parameter (currently none, so the hook only performs tier-coherence and reservation). A comment in the plugin plus this 5-Whys record the Codex rejection so a future session does not re-add the parameter.
verification: The existing reservation path still rejects over-budget dispatches (usage-ledger tests 43/43 pass, cost-router plugin tests 3/3 pass); after removing the wire-parameter set, a live opencode dispatch to openai/gpt-5.6-luna succeeded (2026-09-05T00:13:06Z, response "OPENAI_WIRE_FIXED"), the reservation ledger metered the request (rolling 24h used 141.04 of 200 soft cap), and the provider state remains available/allowed.
